items.author: pizzaforfree.itch.io
items.context: Itch and GOG don't market themselves as game stores the same way Steam and EGS do (did?). They focus on their own branches of the market; GOG for, y'know, good old games, and itch for indie digital media, not just games. They don't compete in the AAA market.
items.text: Fair point. GOG's whole identity is classic games sold DRM-free, so you can keep the installer and back it up, which is a different promise from a launcher-based store.

items.author: corbynred.bsky.social
items.context: I do think re-releasing all the games on GOG (and also on Switch 2 and other Consoles) with patches to remove EA App access and with a way to use DA Keep offline would be good. Remakes though? No. I don't want remakes. We want to preserve all the Dragon Age games DRM-free.
items.text: DRM-free installers really are the best protection for older games: once you have the files backed up, a store or launcher going away doesn't matter.

items.author: calextheneko.bsky.social
items.context: So the game I was trying to get running last night was Morrowind. And I did get it running but have to still fix things to be streamable. At this point I think it's just be easier to pick it up next time it's on sale on steam or gog
items.text: Morrowind can be fiddly on modern PCs, so I get the frustration. If you wait for a sale, look at the game's price history first so you know what a real low looks like.
